verdict.rationale: LiveKit documents self-hosting deployment on your own domain and infrastructure, including an embedded TURN server. A hands-on probe booted the Apache-2.0 livekit-server with no account or key, and another confirmed the open-source livekit-agents framework is pip/npm-installable and imports without a key, so both the open-source runtime and on-prem hosting are evidenced. Missing for 10: a hands-on run of an agent worker connected end-to-end to a self-hosted server, and an explicitly stated open-source license for the Agents framework itself (only the server is shown as Apache-2.0).

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the voice agent runtime from open-source code on my own infrastructure

citations.quote: `livekit-server --dev` (brew-installed, Apache-2.0 OSS) booted on this machine with NO account or key
the open-source agents framework is real and pip-installable
In order to have a secure LiveKit deployment, you will need a domain as well as a SSL certificate for that domain.
LiveKit includes an embedded TURN server. It's a secure TURN implementation that has integrated authentication with the rest of LiveKit.
LiveKit is an open-source platform for building voice, video, and physical AI agents.
